name: AI QA Release Risk Assessment (synthetic REQ-BEN-001)

meta.description: Orchestration only. Each node shells out to src/pipelineCli.ts, which delegates to the existing Phase 2-5 components. No QA risk rules and no release-decision rules are defined in this workflow. The Phase 3 deterministic release gate is the sole decision authority. Run n8n with the repository root as the working directory. Optional environment (never stored here): GEMINI_API_KEY for the live Gemini step, or PIPELINE_AGENT_FINDINGS_FILE=./workflows/sample-agent-findings.json for an offline demo run.

nodes.name: Manual Trigger
nodes.notes: Start a single assessment run for the one synthetic scenario.

nodes.name: Retrieve QA Data (MCP)
nodes.notes: Phase 4: calls the four read-only MCP tools (get_requirement, get_existing_tests, get_known_defects, get_risk_rules) via src/mcpServer.ts.

nodes.name: AI Reasoning
nodes.notes: Phase 5: Gemini 3.6 Flash performs the 7 analysis steps and returns structured findings + a human-readable explanation. It does NOT decide the release. Uses GEMINI_API_KEY, or PIPELINE_AGENT_FINDINGS_FILE for an offline recorded-output run.

nodes.name: Validate Structured Findings
nodes.notes: Phase 5: validateAgentFindings() — rejects malformed / incomplete output and any LLM-supplied decision field. Failure here makes the gate fail safe.

nodes.name: Deterministic Adapter
nodes.notes: Phase 5: adaptAgentFindingsToReleaseFindings() — builds the Phase 3 release-findings object from authoritative dataset facts plus the deterministic security-severity projection; grounding checks fail safe.

nodes.name: Deterministic Release Gate
nodes.notes: Phase 3: the ONLY step that produces a decision. Runs the deterministic release gate; no decision rules are defined here or anywhere in this workflow.

nodes.name: Assemble Release Report
nodes.notes: Copies fields into the final report: release decision, fired rule, reasons (from the gate step verbatim), plus AI explanation, identified risks, coverage assessment, regression priorities, and the pipeline trace.
